rationale: Every PO-03 command-line entry point, enumerated so the subprocess-boundary harness runs all of them rather than a convenient subset. A harness that discovers its own targets can quietly stop covering one; a declared list makes an omission visible as a diff.

clean_environment.policy: The child inherits nothing. PATH is rebuilt from os.defpath plus the interpreter's own directory, LC_ALL is pinned, and HOME and TMPDIR are redirected into a per-run scratch tree outside the repository.
clean_environment.why_not_a_filtered_copy: Filtering the parent environment leaves whatever the filter's author did not think of. Constructing the environment from nothing means a new inherited dependency shows up as a failure instead of as a pass that happens to work on this machine.

invocations.name: check-workflows
invocations.expect_stdout_contains: no cache, no install and no secret

entry_points.bytecode_note: The default mode also checks the checkout for warm bytecode. It is not exercised here because the harness runs from a tree in which the suite has already run, so caches exist by then; the workflow runs that mode before anything imports.

entry_points.network_note: Only the argument surface is exercised. A real invocation clones from the remote, which would make this harness network-dependent and slow; the clone is covered by unit a3-u01's committed transcript and by the clean-runner workflow.

invocations.name: scan-owned-paths
invocations.scope_note: Scoped from the whole tree to my own directory. What this harness proves is that the entry point runs as a separate process and reaches the exit code its contract promises. Pointing it at the whole tree made that claim depend on whether every other cohort's files happen to be clean, so a routed finding in a7's module would read as a process-boundary failure. The whole-tree claim is asserted in test_a3_hermeticity, where it is currently and truthfully red.

entry_points.network_note: Same reason as clean_clone: the substantive modes need baseline reachability and a network namespace, both covered by unit a3-u06.

entry_points.recursion_note: Only --help is exercised. Running the harness inside itself would nest indefinitely, and the harness's substantive behaviour is covered by test_a3_process_boundary.py.

invocations.name: help
invocations.expect_stdout_contains: route PO-03 gate findings to their owners

entry_points.declared_by_note: Declared here, not modified. The manifest is mine and the tool is a11's. A harness that only covers its author's entry points proves nothing about the boundary, so a --help invocation is declared for every committed entry point in the tree. Only the read-only invocation is declared: this tool mutates shared custody state, so running it for real inside a test would be a write no test is entitled to make.

invocations.name: help
invocations.expect_stdout_contains: ingest a wave of subordinate results

recorded_boundaries.statement: python3 -I implies -E, so every PYTHON* variable is ignored, including PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE. Suppressing __pycache__ in an isolated child requires the -B flag; setting the environment variable has no effect.
recorded_boundaries.consequence: A clean-clone run that set PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE and asserted a pristine tree failed, because the suite wrote bytecode caches anyway.
recorded_boundaries.fix: clean_clone.sh passes -B for its pristine-tree pass and classifies bytecode separately for the canonical pass.

recorded_boundaries.statement: make_result.main() takes no parameters and reads sys.argv directly, unlike every other PO-03 entry point whose main() accepts an argv list. It can only be driven as a command; calling main(args) in-process raises TypeError.
recorded_boundaries.observed_in: a3-u08 harness with --compare: make_result:help and make_result:emit are subprocess_only_successes
recorded_boundaries.consequence: Any future in-process orchestration of PO-03 tools must special-case make_result or invoke it as a subprocess. The harness reports this as a boundary rather than a defect, because the subprocess form is the form CI and reviewers use.

recorded_boundaries.statement: workstreams/po03 has no __init__.py and is not on sys.path, so no entry point can be reached by import in a clean clone. python3 -I -m unittest workstreams.po03.tests.test_a3_clean_clone fails with ModuleNotFoundError; only discovery by directory works.
recorded_boundaries.observed_in: a3-u01, first attempt to run a single test module by dotted name
recorded_boundaries.consequence: Any harness that reached these modules by import would be testing something a clean runtime cannot do. Every module here is loaded by file path with importlib instead.

recorded_boundaries.statement: python3 -I also implies -P, so the script's own directory is not prepended to sys.path. A script run as `python3 -I script.py` cannot import a module sitting beside it: `import probe_module` raises ModuleNotFoundError even with probe_module.py in the same directory.
recorded_boundaries.observed_in: a3-u08, while building the PO03-BOUNDARY-001 reproduction: the probe script failed on its sibling import before it ever got as far as testing bytecode suppression
recorded_boundaries.consequence: Sibling imports are unavailable under the mandated -I interpreter flag. Loading by explicit importlib spec is the only portable route, which is what every PO-03 test does. It also means the PO03-BOUNDARY-001 reproduction had to load its probe module by path rather than by name.
